[Spoiler=[b][u]Last Days of the Republic - Assault on Strip 95 airport - Post 3[/u][/b]]

[i]A drone passes in front of the afternoon sun, circling hundreds of feet above the evacuated airport. Passengers waiting for their flights either took off on the last planes that departed or are somewhere on the island, hunkered in basements and hoping for safety.  The little activity seen through the drones powerful camera were a few guards which wouldnt be out of place on a normal day, perhaps ordered to stay here to make sure nobody tries to ransack the place. The activity in the tiedown area is what drew the most attention. A sole airplane sat near the private parking area, being loaded with boxes and miscellaneous items by what looked to civilians. This was good. The battle in the islands capital and the enemy prioritizing the protection of their SMBMs left this airport wide open apart from its guards and a small mobile AA battery a few clicks away, making it perfect target to capture, they would just need to deal with that SPAA battery before they could get anything in here. 

Leaving the drone operator's side at his operating station, the commander of the battalion peaks into the drivers cab.[/i] Let's get this show on the road! Nothin but security guards and some people tryna evac. 

[i]He returns to the command module of his Cougar and taps the radioman on the shoulder. [/i]

I want Jackson, Exal, and Anka to take their squads and sweep the terminals. Martin and his men take the control tower. Everyone else fans out and secures the main airfield. We expect little resistance, and tell them dont fire unless fired upon. I dont want to have to explain why we used the 20mm against a security guard with a pistol. Prisoners are better. 

[i]Getting a nod from the radioman, he sits back in his seat and waits for the radioman to rattle off the orders before getting on the vehicles internal channel.[/i] 

Driver, take us forward till we see that plane. Were intercepting this flight.

[i]MRAV and PLSV engines rumbled as the vehicles moved tediously through the small stretch of forest still between them and the airport, infantry following closely behind. As soon as the vehicles reached the clearing however, they accelerated as fast as possible, making beelines to the closest gate or security entrance in sight. One vehicle blew through a boom barrier, nearly blowing through the security shed meant to check if the person going through was authorized to be there. Splitting and heading to their own destinations, the vehicles left space for the infantry to move in, two men stopping to secure the hyperventilating security guard on the ground who just had his life flash before his eyes. 

Speeding past the parked aircraft, the commanders MRAV finally spotted the aircraft, people rushing around it panicked. If it was getting ready for takeoff, they werent gonna let it. After making a rather abrupt turn for the armored car, the driver came to a stop about ten feet away from the nose of the plane and the 20mm cannon mounted atop the vehicle swiveled around and focused on the aircraft, ready to punch through the thin aluminum body at a moments notice. The three people who were loading the plane stopped what they were doing. After the small infantry element of the commanders squad unloaded from the vehicle, they identified them as two men, one woman, all human. The men immediately put their hands up, while the woman stood frozen with a small box in her arms. [/i]

Tell her to put the box down slowly and put her hands up. [i]one of the infantry men ordered. Before one of the men could gather a response, the woman did as requested. [/i]

[i]Hopping out of the MRAV, the commander walked up to the men.[/i] Whats your reason for this flight? [i]he asked in a curious yet commanding tone, eyeing the aircraft suspiciously. [/i]

Who the hell are you guys? Is this some DSI setup? [i]one of the men askes, halfway confused, halfway angry.[/i]

Nah we aint part of your governments shady little spy agency. Much too tedious for me. I could never stand playing a fake life for years. Again, whats in the plane? [i]The commander checks behind him to see how his men are doing. No gunshots yet, so that's a good sign.[/i]

"Hey, can you help me here!" [i]A person shouts from inside the plane.[/i] "You know these test subjects. Make sure Ukkat doesn't try to escape. HEY, DO YOU HEAR ME? [i]As the man inside continues to shout, the three outside get increasingly more and more nervous.
[/i]
[i]One of the men outside decides to finally say something. [/i]"John, code 097!" [i]The phrase immediately prompts the 20mm gun mounted on the MRAV to focus on the cargo hold of the plane, and results in the man getting a buttstock to the stomach.[/i]

[i]A side door on the plane opens, revealing a man whose expression goes from angry to shocked the second he sees the soldiers. His shock doesn't freeze him though, as he quickly grabs a hold of something inside the plane and pulls it in front of him, revealing it to be an anthro child.[/i] Dont move! I swear to God Ill put a hole in it! t[i]he man yells, a pistol pointed at the child's head. 
[/i]
[i]The commander looks at the man, furrowing his brow and putting his hand on his radio. He holds his hand up, saying[/i] Did you really have to go and make this harder for all of us? How about you put the gun down and release the kid, then we might let you fly off [i]While the man is distracted by his words and held up hand, the commander clicks the little transmit button on his radio three times, still on the vehicle radio channel.[/i]

"So, Lavins sent their special forces? You know this will trigger a much worse conflict." [i]He looks towards his comrade. [/i]

"I wasn't looking to make this harder, but if you damn liberals care about these things. I will make sure he will be left dead!" Slowly, he walks out of the plane, still holding the child at gunpoint. Unfortunately for him however, the sound of the MRAV mounted 20MM signaled his mistake. An APDS round ripped through his upper torso at supersonic speeds, splattering him over the tarmac. 

The child stands stunned for a second before starting to cry. 

Poor sod. [i]The commander turns to the two soldiers and points at the three remaining operators of whatever this flight was.[/i] Restrain those three. Me and the driver will inspect the aircraft. 

[i]The commander walks up to the kid and consoles him, eventually picking him up and setting him inside the MRAV.[/i] Listen buddy, its gonna be okay. Weve got you. [i]The commander reaches into his pocket and pulls out a tube of chocolate discs from one of his MREs and gives it to the kid, calming him down a bit. [/i]

[i]Eventually, the airport is secure and the aircraft is inspected. Boxes of documents, vials, and numerous unidentified items all related to bio-testing. After informing Lavian intelligence, the aircraft is taken to a hangar on the airport until intelligence operatives can arrive and transport the plane back to Makinar to be inspected.

Later in the day, the commander receives great news. After a short battle, a sizable port and town nearby has been captured. Now all they need to do is start shipments coming in and take out that pesky SPAA battery thatll prevent them from flying anything in or out.
[/i][/spoiler]
